title: Studying Scripture
definition: Studying Scripture is the faithful practice of reading, observing, interpreting, and applying the written Word of God with reverence, humility, prayer, and obedience.
summary: God gave Scripture so His people may know Him, trust His promises, recognize His will, discern truth from error, and be equipped for faithful living. Bible study is not merely gathering information; it is sitting under God's authority and responding to His Word.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the center and fulfillment of Scripture. He taught that the Scriptures testify about Him, and true study should lead the heart to behold Christ, trust the Gospel, and follow Him in obedience.

studySections.heading: Why Scripture Must Be Studied
studySections.content: Scripture is God's breathed-out Word and is profitable for teaching, correction, reproof, and training in righteousness. The believer studies Scripture because God has spoken, and His Word is trustworthy, sufficient, and necessary for spiritual growth.

studySections.heading: How to Study Scripture Faithfully
studySections.content: Faithful study asks what the passage says, what it means in context, what it reveals about God and Christ, and how it calls the reader to believe, repent, obey, worship, or persevere.

studySections.heading: Study and Obedience Belong Together
studySections.content: The goal of Bible study is not pride, argument, or information alone. The Word is meant to be received with humility and practiced with faith. A hearer who refuses obedience has not truly honored the message of Scripture.

studySections.heading: Role in Discipleship
studySections.content: Studying Scripture strengthens discernment, deepens prayer, shapes doctrine, equips service, and helps believers mature as disciples of Jesus Christ.
